claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with:

**How many children do you have that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (or more) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period, or do they live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand this situation a bit better:

**How many weeks has Alex been in local authority care, and does Alex spend any regular time at home with you each week (for example, at least 24 hours per week or specific overnight stays)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 12 weeks now. Unfortunately, Alex doesn't come home to stay with me - they're at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while Alex is in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the details of what the council is paying for Alex's care arrangements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 8 years old and you live in the UK, which normally meets the basic requirements
- However, Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks and doesn't come home for regular visits

**The challenge:**
According to the rules, when a child is in care for more than 8 weeks, you usually stop being entitled to Child Benefit. There are some exceptions, but a key factor is whether the local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Since you're unsure about what the council is paying for, I cannot definitively determine your eligibility.

**What you should do:**
I recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly. They can:
- Help you understand what the local council is paying for Alex's care
- Advise you on whether any exceptions apply in your specific situation
- Guide you on whether you can claim or continue claiming Child Benefit

You can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office by phone or through their online services. They'll be able to give you a definitive answer based on the full details of Alex's care arrangement.
